subject: history_social
notes: In 1935 psychologist John Ridley Stroop published a study of how people name colors.
In his task, people see color words printed in colored ink and must name the ink color, not read the word.
When the word and the ink match (the word "red" printed in red ink), people respond quickly.
When they conflict (the word "red" printed in blue ink), people respond more slowly and make more errors.
Psychologists interpret this pattern as a sign that skilled readers process words automatically, even when they try not to.
The Stroop task is now one of the most widely used tests in psychology.
stem: The student wants to introduce the Stroop task to an audience unfamiliar with it. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: The Stroop task, published in 1935, has become one of the most widely used tests in psychology.
choices.B: Psychologists interpret the Stroop effect as a sign that skilled readers process words automatically, even when they are trying not to read them.
choices.C: People respond more slowly and make more errors when the word "red" is printed in blue ink than when it is printed in red ink.
choices.D: In the Stroop task, first described by psychologist John Ridley Stroop in 1935, people must name the ink color of printed color words, a job that becomes harder when the word names a different color.

explanation.why: An audience unfamiliar with the task needs to be told what it is: who introduced it and what people are asked to do. Only one choice both names the task and explains the procedure. The others assume the reader already knows what the task involves.
explanation.A: Incorrect. It says the task is widely used but not what it is.
explanation.B: Incorrect. It gives the interpretation of the effect, which only makes sense to someone who already knows the task.
explanation.C: Incorrect. It reports a result of the task but never says what the task is, so an unfamiliar reader could not follow it.
explanation.D: Correct. It names the task, its originator, and what participants must do, which is exactly what a newcomer needs.
